title: Getting Started with Product and Engineering in Strawberry
description: Connect customer evidence, product specs, metrics, browser-based QA, and grounded bug reports without losing the reasoning between steps.
introduction: Product work often loses its reasoning as it moves. Customer feedback becomes a theme without its source. A theme becomes a spec without an explicit decision. The thing that ships is then judged by a dashboard whose definitions nobody checked.

Engineering has a related gap: the observed product behavior, browser evidence, team discussion, recent code changes, and final ticket often live in different places. Strawberry can work across those real surfaces, remember accepted context, and keep the evidence connected while the team remains in control of consequential actions.

sections.title: See the connected Product and Engineering system

blocks.text: Bring the product question, customer feedback, critical flow, metric, or unexpected behavior that matters now. Strawberry can recommend a few relevant starting points and complete one result the team can inspect while keeping both Product learning and Engineering quality in view.

rows: Customer evidence → accepted problem → product specification → metric definition and review.
Observed behavior → bounded browser audit → grounded issue → requested fix and proportionate validation.

blocks.text: The companion can move through visible browser tabs and logged-in tools, follow links into the underlying source, and let a teammate observe or take over. Evidence can continue into an approved document or issue without another copy-and-paste handoff.

sections.title: Move from feedback to an accepted product definition

blocks.text: Feedback synthesis should preserve the situation around the comment: who encountered the problem, in which flow or version, with what outcome, and how representative the source can be. Strawberry keeps themes, tensions, examples, gaps, and confidence connected to the underlying records. A thin sample produces questions and evidence gaps, not an automatic roadmap rank.

Once the team accepts the problem, the product spec can define users, outcomes, requirements, flows, edge cases, dependencies, open questions, and acceptance criteria. It describes the product behavior to create without quietly deciding architecture or implementation on Engineering's behalf.

sections.title: Define the measure before reading the chart

blocks.text: A product metric is only useful when the behavior, population, numerator, denominator, time window, source, and exclusions are clear. Strawberry can define the smallest metric framework a decision needs, reconcile competing dashboard definitions, and review baselines, trends, funnels, cohorts, segments, guardrails, and data quality.

Observed movement, plausible explanation, and product implication remain separate. When the work requires substantial SQL, joins, statistics, or validation, shared Data capabilities can own that layer while Product keeps the decision and metric meaning. Instrumentation changes stay with Engineering.

items.context: Define the metric framework, review supported performance, and make the gaps and implications clear.

sections.title: Test the product and ground the bug report

blocks.text: A Product Flow Audit actually navigates the experience. It checks the critical path and the few variations most likely to reveal a material problem, then returns passes, regressions, screenshots, relevant console or network evidence, exclusions, and uncertainty. Public live sites are appropriate for read-only inspection; authenticated or stateful paths belong in staging, preview environments, or dedicated test accounts when possible.

When a finding is a real bug, Strawberry can connect that evidence to approved Slack or Teams discussion, GitHub context and recent changes, logs, existing issues, and the team's actual ticketing system. It searches for a duplicate before preparing or filing the issue. If the user also wants a fix, the companion can continue through the available coding workflow under the normal repository and validation boundaries.

items.context: Navigate and test a critical flow, then return inspectable browser evidence.
Research unexpected behavior, find duplicates, and prepare or file a grounded issue within scope.

blocks.text: Product and engineering work still depends on the shared operating layer. Meeting preparation and debrief keep decisions attached to their records. Open-loop reviews reconcile commitments and ownership across systems. Status updates turn the accepted view into the right message for leadership or the team. Onboarding gives a new teammate a role-aware path through current work instead of a document dump.

After one of these methods has worked, a shared-team workflow can preserve its sources, owners, destination, privacy boundaries, and review behavior. Keep every external action distinct: product testing does not approve a ticket, a ticket does not approve a code change, and a code change does not approve merging, deployment, production data changes, or customer communication.
